structure: A ruling file, workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-10-09.md, 260 lines. It opens with Sam's verbatim words: one quote of 8 October (the prototype decides look and feel, not architecture; page duplication via feature folders is desired; option B of germinal/options.md) and eleven quoted answers of 9 October (germinal typeCode, what the germinal notification sends to PIMS, germinal links landing early, germinal E2E specs in the animals project, rows waiting on MDM, stub tidy-up, port of exit, port order and rail, MDM country block, c-218, c-217 address search, when an animal counts as identified). A paragraph then explains that 'option B plan' claims stand because option B was chosen, and that the port findings were checked against MDM raw captures. Then 40 numbered claims the main session read from the quotes, in eight sections: (a) germinal products is a sibling set, claims 1-15; (b) what the prototype decides, claims 16-19; (c) the URL and architecture findings, claims 20-24; (d) reference lists and MDM, claims 25-33 (claim 30 has four repo sub-bullets); (e) address search, claims 34-35; (f) when an animal counts as identified, claims 36-38; (g) overview-opened pages, claim 39; (h) repos, claim 40. Scope is the whole file, so nothing is left out. The user's request centres on the germinal products set (section (a) and the germinal halves of claims 20-24), but the whole file is in scope and is one part.

parts.title: Whole ruling of 8 and 9 October
parts.scope: The whole file, from the heading to claim 40: the verbatim quotes of 8 and 9 October, the option B explanatory paragraph, and all 40 numbered claims in sections (a) to (h).
covers: The 8 October quote and the 11 quoted answers of 9 October: each claim's quote is taken from these verbatim words, and every listed claim is checked against them (verbatim where the quote says it, inferred or 'option B plan' where it only follows from choosing option B)

The paragraph after the quotes: option B overrules option A's recommendation; 'option B plan' claims stand by the choice of option B; every MDM port carries traffic and none carries an approved-for-animals flag

Section (a), claims 1-15: the germinal-products sibling set (SET_ID, mount, gateway, paths and slugs), page duplication as architecture, the three left-out pages and germinal field differences, one category per set and the 12 catalogue lines moved, GBN-AG references, category stored on the backend record and published to INS, typeCodes SEMEN/EMBRYO/OVA and LIVE_ANIMAL, what is and is not published to PIMS v0.2.0 and EUDPA-686, donor details from the real model, germinal offered and unblocked in INS, early-landing links, type change starting a new notification, the 18 split requirements, the germinal-products theme in the last wave, and E2E specs under tests/animals/{e2e,a11y,security}/germinal-products/

Section (b), claims 16-19: prototype decides look and feel only, never architecture; when an architecture change is adopted; no existing URL path or code structure changes; acceptance criteria assert pages not paths; the claims of ruling:sam-2026-10-07 each replaces or keeps

Section (c), claims 20-24: every dropped requirement, increment and conflict in claim 20; every content-kept-without-URL item in claim 21; every kept-for-a-constraint item in claim 22; every unchanged item in claim 23; template mode types in claim 24 — each req, inc and c id named

Section (d), claims 25-33: no list waits on MDM; destination and transit country lists from GBNAG_SPS_EX with subdivisions; inc-008 and inc-082 unblocked; each list keeps its MDM block; the stub tidy-up row and its four repo sub-bullets (trade-imports-stub, animals frontend, ins frontend, ins tests) with dependent increments; port of exit offers the whole list; duplicates and misspellings are MDM data; port traffic mapped and ordered airports, seaports, rail
Section (e), claims 34-35: address search blocked on the lookup becoming a real feature, the blocked rows, manual entry built now, re-distil later, and the Northern Ireland search blocked with it
Section (f), claims 36-38: one identifier is enough, DR1 inc-103 closed and inc-147's blocker removed, the multi-line rule written into openspec
Section (g), claim 39: overview-opened pages return to the overview, inc-002 criterion 10 removed, no ?from=hub marker

Gap claims for anything the ruling touches but leaves open, such as the schema shape for EUDPA-686, the airport/seaport flag ticket the quote asked for versus claim 33's 'no future ticket', and the content of the future address-search re-distil
